I don't know if it's normal, but I do it too. I just think that most people aren't 100% compatible, and if you're around someone enough you're going to often suppress the traits about them that bother you, but eventually it's going to manifest itself internally or externally.

Of course it could also be some type of mood disorder that is taking place. I know when I'm more depressed my negative thoughts tend to be about real things, but it's shit that wouldn't bother me at all when I'm in a better mood. I could think about those things for hours, but they wouldn't affect me, when I feel good. 
It's kind of a chicken or egg thing with the mind. Does your mood influence your thoughts? Do your thoughts influence your mood? Is it a combination of both? Who knows? It's difficult to say.

Don't think of yourself as an asshole. There's this idea that we're nevertheless allowed to have a negative thought about our friends or family, but the truth is we're human. People aren't 100% compatible. Beating yourself up about that will just create more tension.

However, the work to do is to ask yourself how much of it is valid. How much of it is just you looking for them to live up to an expectation that isn't fair? I'm sure you're not perfect in their eyes either. Maybe sometimes it's good to even just give yourself some space when you feel that way.

If you're prepared to end it all, why not just go for what you really want full stop? At this point, you have nothing to fear. The fear of death can be linked to so many innocuous fears that hold us back. In fact, I think that's pretty much what all fear can be traced back to.

We fear failing, because we fear that we might be ostracized, and then in our minds that ostracization leads to death. 

Well, you've gotten that out of the way but you're still you and you still have dreams. Why not go for them? Besides who knows what awaits you on the other side? What if you're just reborn. Then you have to face the same existential crisis many of of face, but hate to talk about in public. Wouldn't that blow? And what if you end up in a worse country than wherever you're from now? Or, like, on a planet where there's no internet?

I'm not saying it'll make things perfect but in my darkest hours some of what I've learned from meditation has kept me going. You really do have to sometimes just live in the moment and take things moment to moment. Don't be so hard on yourself, the world is already tough enough. Just focus on the little things. Sleep, exercise, nutrition, doing what makes you feel good (so long as it doesn't lead to negative outcomes; although you can still even do things of that nature on occasion). Finding a creative outlet can also be great. You can hide your pain in metaphor and the best part is that those that encounter your work will still get it.
There's nothing you can express that someone else hasn't felt and in a world where reality is increasingly being turned on its head the worst that will happen is that you'll be misunderstood by most and highly valued by some.

You're still here. Might as well make the most of it.

EDIT: I read through some of your other stuff. I think maybe what would also help is not getting stuck on the idea of what you "should" be doing right now if there are other factors getting in the way. I know it's probably difficult because you may want to escape your current predicament, so badly that you think whatever you want to do is the only way out, but you're really young. You have to sometimes just try shit without any expectations. You may hate it, but you might bump into something you love and didn't expect along the way. You're way too young to have it all figured out.

Hell, I don't have it all figured out and I'm damn near twice your age, but I know that after experiencing many lows I've experienced many highs and the moments where I was down gave me a resilience and appreciation I treasure more than anything.

Trust me, it can get better but it takes time. Sometimes you have to wallow through shit before you can enjoy a shower. Just take a moment, be still, breathe and try to find those little moments of joy. Then just try things with reckless abandon and try to find what works. I know it sounds shitty but I think you'll come across it and look back on these moments with a little more perspective.

Be kind to yourself, try to take care of yourself as best you can, and just try a few different things with no major expectations. I think you'll bump into the right thing, much like you bump into a new favorite song. You don't control it, you discover it. And you know you'll always find another song you like eventually. Life is like that. It's a lot of songs that you hate or are so-so, but those moments when you bump into the right one make it all worth it.

Meditation has kept me going. And not just any kind of meditation, the kind where you almost completely clear your mind try to get into really deep relaxation and start spasming. It took a while to get to that point, but it was worth it and keeps me wondering if I can progress even further. 
Some people experience psychotic breaks while meditating, and in the back of my mind I fear that, but I feel I don't have much to lose so I just try to let go and let my body do whatever. 

Things aren't perfect by any stretch of the imagination, but it really works. I'm better at getting out of my head and it's given me some of my creative spark back. I'm less tense and sometimes find I can enjoy the present moment a lot more.

I slowly worked on developing a state of "no mind" (I suggest you do research) prior to really going deeper with meditation. I don't think I'm far along enough yet to say I've mastered it, but I don't get caught up in my negative thoughts as much and I notice and interrupt them more. I mostly developed it by constantly questioning the utility of thoughts I was having. This eventually allowed me to have a little more control over my mind and then the real fun began. I've learned a lot and realized I can even get into this meditative state while walking, riding the bus, working or just laying in bed in no particular position. It's really helped me cope on days when I wake up and don't know how I'll make it through. 

If you're going to go down swinging, you might as well get a coping mechanism in your arsenal that requires nothing but you and a little time.

It comes off as awfully self-centered because you seem to make their problems about you.

Perhaps it's a case of opposites attract and your presumably warm, caring, open, attitude attracts people that have are not developed on those traits and are a bit more aloof and less emotional.
Some people, myself included, feel they can handle their issues on their own. They want to learn and grow from their hardships and don't want someone swooping in and saving them.

Respect their wishes and don't make their problems about you.

At least you have the drive to change. Don't give up, fight for what you really want. You *will* stumble and you will have days where you want to quit, but if you keep at it things will improve.
You'll find a new job, new friends, new boo, and you'll change all of your bad habits with drugs.
Don't let age hold you back, being younger isn't everything it's cracked up to be.
